synth.generative_prior:
Computable defaults per Solen customer-surface class (dashboard excluded, already sourced via TASTE_DASHBOARDS):

1. SEARCH RESULTS / LIST (scan-many mode, structure-locked to Fresha): card = 1 image (single photo or carousel) + name (14px semibold) + rating value + distance/address line + category tag + review count. NO price, NO per-card CTA button, NO inline service preview. Density band: mobile ~1.2-1.5 cards visible per 812px fold (near full-bleed photo card, ~480-560px tall); desktop 2-column card grid inside a ~700px list column alongside a persistent (not force-collapsed) map, ~4 cards visible above an ~900px fold. Grounded in: Fresha search (measured live this session, fresha.com/search, both viewports) which is Solen's locked STRUCTURE source per the dual-axis rule, cross-checked against Airbnb's list+map split (CONV, ~18 results/grid beside a persistent map) which independently converges on the same list+map pattern. Booksy's thicker card (rating+distance+badge+3 inline priced services, ~8-10 fields/card, T1 measured) and ClassPass's denser 4-rows-with-status-chip pattern (T2, Mobbin) are named as the DENSER alternative Solen should NOT adopt, since Solen's locked "no times in listings, no fabricated price preview on a card" rules already side with Fresha's thin-row philosophy.

2. DISCOVERY / INSPO FEED (scan-many, visual-first mode): 2-column masonry (matches the existing project north-star of a Pinterest-style gallery), gutter target 8-12px (between Pinterest's near-zero gutter and Cosmos's ~8-10px breathing-room gutter), NO text-caption scrim overlay on tiles (Lemon8's dark-gradient caption pattern is richer/more graphic than Solen's flat 80/17 no-hype surface law allows), save-affordance limited to a small corner icon (Pinterest's "+" pattern). Density band: 3+ rows (6+ tiles) visible per 812px mobile fold, matching Pinterest's measured ~3.3 rows (T2, Mobbin) but with Cosmos's calmer gutter (T2, Mobbin) rather than Pinterest's near-zero one, since Pinterest's tightness reads as commercial-volume optimization Solen doesn't need.

3. PDP (decide-on-one mode, low density, generous padding): name (large, 2-line max) then a grey meta line (hours/address) then a bold availability/social-proof line then an action-button row then H2 section headers then content rows at ~90-100px each with a hairline divider, no photo per row for list-style content (e.g. services). Grounded in Square Go's salon PDP (T2, Mobbin, the most directly comparable competitor to Solen's own PDP), which is measurably lower-density and more generously spaced than any list/search/discovery surface in the same app family.

CROSS-CUTTING FORMULA: as a surface moves deeper into the funnel (discovery/search → PDP), density should step DOWN, meaning fields-per-card/row shrinks going INTO a scan surface and padding-per-item grows going INTO a decide surface. No app sampled uses one flat density constant across surface types; treat "one spacing scale, applied identically everywhere" as the anti-pattern this stream corrects, not the 4-pt spacing SCALE itself (which stays locked, only its per-surface application band is new).

synth.principle_summary: Information density is not one constant Solen should apply everywhere. It steps down as the customer moves from scanning many options to deciding on one: search-result and discovery-feed surfaces (scan-many mode) default to compact, image-led cards with few fields, no price, and no per-card CTA; the PDP (decide-on-one mode) default to generous padding, a single top-to-bottom hierarchy, and no per-row photography. The computable signal is rows-or-tiles-visible-per-viewport-fold together with fields-per-card: both should shrink on scan surfaces and the padding-per-item should grow as the surface approaches the commit action. No real app sampled uses a flat density constant across surface types, and Solen's own locked structure source (Fresha) and closest same-category rival (Booksy) actively disagree on search-card density, which is itself evidence that "density" is a per-surface decision, not a single number.
synth.proposed_addition:
## Density defaults per customer surface (generative prior, tag: generative-gap)

**Gap this fills:** Solen's dashboard density is already sourced (see TASTE_DASHBOARDS); customer-facing surfaces (search results, Inspo/discovery feed, PDP) had no computable density prior, so a new surface risked being eyeballed rather than derived. This section is that prior.

**Prior (bands, not frozen literals, since none of these touch an already-LOCKFILE'd row directly):**
- Search results / list: thin Fresha-style row (photo + name + rating + distance + category/reviews, no price, no per-card CTA), mobile ~1.2-1.5 cards/fold, desktop ~4 cards/fold in a 2-col grid beside a persistent (not forced) map.
- Inspo / discovery feed: 2-col masonry, 8-12px gutter, no caption scrim on tiles, ~3+ rows/fold on mobile.
- PDP: generous padding, single hierarchy (name -> meta -> availability/social proof -> actions -> sectioned content), ~90-100px content rows with hairline dividers, no per-row photography for list content.
- Formula: density steps DOWN with funnel depth (scan surfaces = fewer fields, higher row count; decide surface = fewer rows, more padding per item). Do not apply one flat spacing constant across all three.

**Named real-app anchors (so a builder has a concrete image, not just a number):** Fresha search (Solen's own structure source, thin-card, measured), Booksy search (thick price-led card, explicitly the pattern to AVOID for search results), Square Go PDP (closest generously-spaced PDP analog), Pinterest / Cosmos masonry (discovery feed structure vs Solen-appropriate gutter restraint).

**Explicitly rejected, do not adopt:** per-card CTA buttons on search rows (KAYAK, Klook pattern; conflicts with Solen's ink-only single-commit-button rule), price/service preview baked into the search card (Booksy pattern; conflicts with no-times-in-listings and no-fabricated-price-preview rules), dark-gradient caption scrims on discovery tiles (Lemon8 pattern; conflicts with the 80/17 no-decorative-overlay law).

**Tensions noted, NOT applied (owner reopening required, not this stream's call):** 2026 trend material describes "fluid spacing over fixed margins" and "density that expands with user proficiency" (T3, trade-press). Both would require touching Solen's locked 4-pt spacing scale (V3-D443) or building a net-new personalization system; flagged here as background context only, per the precedence chain (LOCKFILE outranks trend research).

**Taste-Lab probe:** show the owner two live-mockup variants of the search-results list at the same data set: (A) Fresha-anchored thin row (photo + name + rating + distance + category, no price) at the ~1.3-cards/mobile-fold band, vs (B) a denser Booksy-style row with an inline lowest-price service preview. Ask which reads as "Solen" and why, to lock the search-card field count as a LOCKFILE row rather than leave it as this stream's unlocked prior.

myths_caught: The draft's central T1 claim ('Fresha search card structure and density bands', sourced to 'fresha.com/search, live-rendered this session') is factually inverted. Live re-check this pass of the SAME session's already-open Fresha tabs (tab-3 and tab-8, both at the real /search results view with '9 venues within map area' + Filters + persistent map, screenshotted at 800x450) shows each search-result card actually carries: photo carousel + name + distance/address + category + (rating when present) + THREE inline priced/duration services (e.g. 'Haarschnitt, 30 min, CHF 40') + a 'View N matching services' link. That is a price-led, service-preview card, structurally closer to what the draft itself labels 'the Booksy pattern Solen should reject' than to the thin no-price card the draft describes. The thin card (photo + name + rating + address + category + review count, no price) is real, but it is Fresha's HOMEPAGE recommendation carousel (fresha.com root, confirmed via tab-1), not its search-results page.

Because of the inversion above, the draft's 'Booksy ~8-10 fields/card vs Fresha ~5 fields/card (rejected-density contrast)' number is backwards: the actual Fresha search card is at least as field-dense as Booksy's (name + distance + category + up to 3 priced/timed services + a service-count link), not the sparse 5-field baseline claimed.

Pinterest '~3.3 rows (6-7 tiles) visible per 812px fold' is presented as if pixel-measured. Mobbin screen captures (re-pulled this pass) support 'roughly 3 rows' qualitatively but not a decimal-precision figure; the '.3' reads as false precision dressed as a measurement, not an actual measurement.
